
## Proposed shape

Add to the DSL (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`) and the core `Signals` object:

```kotlin
// Global / fully-qualified topic
fun <T> topic(name: String, initial: T): Signal<T>

// Topic scoped to a subject (customer, order, conversation, …)
fun <T> topic(name: String, subject: Any, initial: T): Signal<T>
```

That gives you both styles, and your original snippet still works:

```kotlin
val consumed = topic("events.consumed", 0L)                       // key = "events.consumed"
val name     = topic("customer.name", customerId, initialName)    // key = ("customer.name", customerId)

// Same thing, fully qualified if you prefer composing it yourself:
val name     = topic("customer.$customerId.name", initialName)
```

```java
hub.publish("events.consumed", count);
hub.publish("customer.name", customerId, updatedName);
```

## What it returns

A read-only `Signal<T>`, backed by a session-local mirror:

```kotlin
Text(name)                                   // Text(Signal<String>)
ForEach(orders) { OrderCard(it) }            // ForEach(Signal<List<Order>>)
Text(orders.map { "${it.size} orders" })     // Signal.map
```

`publish` updates the mirror on the session's actor, so existing effects, bindings, and deltas work unchanged. Only sessions that called `topic` with the same key are updated — the lookup is by `(name, subject)`, so it's targeted, not broadcast.

## The tradeoff

This is stringly typed: a typo in `"customer.name"` on one side silently routes nowhere. Mitigations that keep the DX:

- Put topic names in constants next to the domain type:
  ```kotlin
  object CustomerTopics {
      const val NAME = "customer.name"
      const val ORDERS = "customer.orders"
  }
  ```
- `topic<T>` records the payload type on first subscription; a `publish` with the wrong type is rejected and reported via telemetry rather than corrupting the signal.
- Add a `published with zero subscribers` metric (rate-limited debug log in dev) so a mistyped topic is visible.
- If you later want compile-time topic safety, a typed `Topic<T>` wrapper can sit on top without changing the `topic(...)`/`publish(...)` shape.

## Lifecycle and semantics

- Session-scoped; `topic` is idempotent per `(name, subject)`, so calling it in `body()` or as a field is safe.
- `initial` seeds the signal; subsequent changes arrive via `hub.publish`.
- Publishes are coalesced per session (latest-wins) and applied on the actor.
- An `unsubscribe(name, subject)` escape hatch exists; session close drops everything.
- SSR sessions read their local mirror for the first paint but don't register with the hub.

## Implementation delta

- `SessionSubscriptions` + `SessionContext` interfaces in `pathland-view-core` (so `Signals.topic` can resolve the current session without server-core depending on it).
- `Signals.topic` (core static) and top-level `topic` (DSL) delegating to it.
- `PathlandSession` local mirrors, context thread-local around mount/dispatch/drain, hub registration, close cleanup.
- `PathlandSignalHub` registry-scoped; `publish(name, value)` and `publish(name, subject, value)`.
- Starters produce the root-mount hub; `PathlandHost.signalHub(mount)` for multi-app.
- Tests for targeted delivery, coalescing, close cleanup, actor-thread application, Quarkus/Spring background threads; docs/status updates.

 > The canonical core is a **Rust engine** that emits the application's
 > **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding,

 ### The 16-byte Opcode Engine
 
 - Every opcode is exactly **16 bytes**: `Category (1B) | Command ID (1B) | Flags (2B) | A (4B) | B (4B) | C (4B)`, `#[repr(C, packed)]`, little-endian.
 - A 64-byte cache line holds exactly **4 opcodes** → L1-cache-friendly.
 - Opcodes live in a **ring buffer** in linear memory; the guest writes at `writeCursor`, the host reads from `readCursor`; frame boundaries via a monotonic `frameCount` in the header block.
 - **Both directions are binary**: a second **event ring** (host → guest) carries `EVENT`-category opcodes. The renderer writes raw inputs at `eventWriteCursor`; the guest drains them at `eventReadCursor`. Events are 16-byte opcodes through the engine, never a side-channel callback.
 - **Variable-length data** (strings, token paths) lives in a bump **arena**; opcodes reference entries by offset (`[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`), so every opcode stays 16 bytes. A second host-owned **event arena** mirrors this in the host → guest direction (shared-memory event strings, e.g. `TEXT_CHANGED`); over the network, host → guest strings ride the batch's string section.
 - **Window metadata** (`META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA`, field family `TITLE`/`DESCRIPTION`/`LOCALE`) carries the hosting surface's presentation metadata; renderers map it to their own chrome (browser `<title>`/meta description/`<html lang>`, GTK/Qt window title). It is root-scoped and signal-backed, so a route title is a computed over the router. Web-only artifacts (canonical/robots/sitemap) stay host-owned.
 - Spec: **`spec/OPCODE.md`** (primary) + **`spec/CONFORMANCE.md`** (golden vectors). Companion catalogs: **`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`** (views), **`spec/MODIFIERS.md`** (modifiers/properties), **`spec/EVENTS.md`** (events), **`spec/LAYOUT.md`** (frame & layout allocation contract) — draft IDs are allocated there spec-first.
 
 ### Declarative, not positioned (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The engine describes WHAT the UI is — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing,
 > padding, alignment — never WHERE it is. It does not compute layout and does
 > not emit rects.**
 
 - The engine emits **declarative structure** (`TREE` create/delete/insert/remove/move) + **constraint properties** (`PARAMETER` spacing/padding/alignment/FILL/HUG hints).
 - **Native elements everywhere**: each platform's renderer maps the opcode stream onto that platform's native elements — GTK4 widgets on desktop, DOM elements in the browser, HTML server-side — and those native elements lay themselves out. Never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent.
 - **Reactive emission**: emission is diff-based. Only the nodes that changed emit opcodes (property diffs via `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_TEXT`, structural diffs via `TREE` opcodes). An unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes. Signals in the application mark the tree dirty; the engine reconciles.

 controllers (`Button::clicked` → pointer up, `EventControllerMotion` →
 pointer move/enter/leave), emitting events through the same `Pump::send_input`
 path.
 
 `pathland_gtk::run` passes an explicit empty argv to GTK (the process command
 line belongs to the embedding host — e.g. the JVM's `-cp`/`-D` flags — and must
 not be parsed as GTK options).
 
 ### Kotlin JVM authoring DSL (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`, in `lib/java/pathland-view-core`)
 
 The **sole JVM authoring surface**. It is the SwiftUI-like DSL shared by desktop,
 Spring Boot, Quarkus, and web apps. Components and modifiers:
 
 - `View` is an **open Kotlin interface** — the library ships `Text`/`Image`/`Color`/
   `Rectangle`, `VStack`/`HStack`/`ZStack`, `Spacer`, `Button`,
   `TextField(placeholder, WritableSignal<String>)`, `Video` (a
   `MediaController`'s surface), and application code defines its own views by
   extending `Component` or implementing `View`. **Media is a state object, not a
   view** (spec/MEDIA.md): `MediaController` owns the resource + transport as
   signals, a `Video` surface renders it, and **audio has no view** — the app
   binds its own buttons/sliders (`controller.attach()` materializes the
   controller's node once, outside any swapping branch).
 - **SwiftUI-style `body()` / reactive components**: composite views declare
   `View body()`; a signal read there subscribes that component, and a later write
   re-renders only that component and diffs its retained subtree. A signal bound
   to a node stays fine-grained and does not re-run the body. Plain
   `if`/`when`/`for` works; `ForEach` is the reactive list component.
 - **Builders and modifiers**: `VStack(spacing = 8f) { … }`, `Text("hi")`,
   `Button("Save") { … }`, `.padding`, `.frame`, `.fontSize`, `.background`,
   `.buttonStyle(BorderedButtonStyle)`, `.windowMetadata`, navigation intents, and
   the full modifier vocabulary. Styles are Kotlin values
   (`PlainButtonStyle`, `BorderedButtonStyle`, label styles, `NativeVideoStyle`).
 - **Builder scopes**: view blocks take a `PathlandScope` receiver. `PathlandScope`,
   `Navigation.Builder`, and modifier/style `Config` receivers share the
   `@PathlandDsl` marker, so an outer router/config receiver cannot be captured
   implicitly inside a nested view block (compile-time guard only; the
   thread-local `ViewScopes` stack still collects children).
 - **Persisted state**: `Component` provides `val count by state(0)` (auto-keyed
   by property name) or `state(0, "key")`, bound to the session's
   `PersistentState` before the first `body()` render — no annotation processor or
   kapt.
 - **Java hosting**: Java Spring Boot/Quarkus apps remain first-class hosts. A
   Java `PathlandApp` bean returns a Kotlin `View`
   (`return () -> MusicPlayerView.make();`); no Kotlin compiler or authoring DSL is
   needed in the host module. Every reusable Kotlin root exposes a public
   constructor or `@JvmStatic make(...)` factory with Java-friendly types.
 - **Consistency** with `pathland_core::constants` is enforced by the
   emitter/HTML tests (golden byte layout + round-trips).

 ## Project Vision
 
 **Pathland is a cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol** that enables retained-mode UI development with multiple renderer backends. It is **protocol-first**, meaning the protocol specification is the source of truth, not any particular implementation.
 
 **Primary Goal**: Write once, run anywhere - Enable UI code to be written once and deployed across web, mobile, desktop, and embedded platforms through different renderer implementations.
 
 **Status**: The Rust opcode engine (16-byte opcode, ring buffer, arena, diff-based reactive emission) is implemented and tested (`cargo test`). See the Architecture section above.
 
 ---
 
 ## CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLES
 
 ### Principle 1: Renderer Statelessness (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The renderer MUST NOT retain application state.**
 
 - Renderers are **pure functions** of the opcode stream: same opcodes → same output
 - A renderer MAY retain its **rendered-output tree** (id → native element + computed layout) for drawing, hit-testing, and event routing — this is a cache of its own output, not state
 - The renderer MUST NOT retain component property values as business state, application control flow, or anything the application can change without emitting an opcode
 - The application owns the canonical retained UI tree
 - The engine emits **deltas only**; the renderer applies them to its native elements
 
 **Violation of this principle is a bug, not a feature.**
 
 ### Principle 2: Command-Based Protocol (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The protocol transmits tree mutations as a stream of commands, NOT as serialized trees.**
 
 - Each frame is a **batch of delta commands** describing changes
 - Only **actual changes** are transmitted (diff-based reactive emission)
 - Protocol acts like a **VM instruction stream** / ABI
 - Deterministic, linear decoding without schema lookup or reflection
 
 ### Principle 3: Binary Protocol (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The protocol MUST be binary.**
 
 - Open-source, cross-platform binary format
 - Fixed **16-byte instructions** in a ring buffer shared with the host via linear memory
 - Custom instruction-based bytecode, not schema-driven serialization
 - **Both directions are binary**: tree mutations (app → renderer) AND raw-input events (renderer → app) share the same instruction format, so the wire is language- and platform-agnostic

 ### Opcode Format
 
 Every opcode is exactly 16 bytes:
 
 ```
 [Category: u8][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
 ```
 
 See `spec/OPCODE.md` for the full format, ring buffer, arena, and frame lifecycle.
 
 ### Machine-readable protocol manifest
 
 `spec/protocol.tsv` is the target-neutral ID manifest emitted from
 `pathland_core::constants` by `pathland-protocol-manifest` (`cargo run -p
 pathland-protocol-manifest`). It contains only `kind`, `group`, `name`, and
 `value`; each language binding keeps its own representation and validates or
 reads the manifest. There is no Rust→JVM source generation.
 
 The JVM mirror is hand-written and checked by
 `pathland-view-core/src/test/java/.../ProtocolManifestTest`: every manifest row
 must match a Java constant, no extra public numeric constants may exist, and
 `ValueTypes.forProperty` must match `property_value_type`. CI regenerates the
 manifest from Rust and fails on drift.
 
 Engine behavior beyond individual opcodes is specified in `spec/ENGINE.md` and
 enforced by shared self-contained frame traces under `spec/engine-traces/`.
 `pathland-engine-golden` emits them from the Rust engine and the JVM
 `EngineTraceTest` compares its encoded frames byte-for-byte.
 
 ### Categories
 
 | Category | Value | Direction | Description |
 |----------|-------|-----------|-------------|
 | TREE | 0x01 | Guest → Host | Node create/delete/insert/remove/move |
 | PARAMETER | 0x02 | Guest → Host | Constraint properties (spacing, padding, …), design tokens |
 | EVENT | 0x03 | Host → Guest | Raw inputs: pointer down/move/up, key down/up |
 | META | 0x04 | Both | Reset, environment, window metadata |

 ### Key Property IDs
 
 **Stack**: SPACING=0x0001, ALIGNMENT=0x0002, CONTENT_MARGINS=0x0005  
 **Text**: TEXT=0x000A, TEXT_ALIGNMENT=0x000C, LINE_LIMIT=0x000B, TRUNCATION_MODE=0x000D  
 **Style**: COLOR=0x100A, FONT_SIZE=0x1007, FONT_WEIGHT=0x1008, FONT_FAMILY=0x1009, BACKGROUND_COLOR=0x1001, BORDER_WIDTH=0x1003, BORDER_COLOR=0x1004, BORDER_RADIUS=0x1005, OPACITY=0x100D, VISIBLE=0x100E, Z_INDEX=0x100F, CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS=0x1010, PADDING=0x1011, PADDING_TOP/RIGHT/BOTTOM/LEFT=0x1012-0x1015  
 **Special**: WIDTH=0x100B (use -1=FILL, -2=HUG_CONTENT), HEIGHT=0x100C  
 **Semantic**: ROLE=0x2001, STATE=0x2002, ENABLED=0x2003, SELECTED=0x2004, EVENT_LISTENERS=0x2005 (u32 bitmask — which raw events a node wants reported), VALUE=0x2006, MIN_VALUE=0x2007, MAX_VALUE=0x2008, LABEL=0x200A, PROMPT=0x200B  
 **Binding/action**: ACTION_ID=0x2016, BINDING_ID=0x2017, TOGGLE_STYLE=0x2018 (Switch=0, Checkbox=1, Button=2)  
 **Media** (spec/MEDIA.md): MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID=0x103A (a `VIDEO`'s controller), MEDIA_SOURCE=0x103B, MEDIA_MUTED=0x103C, MEDIA_LOOP=0x103D, MEDIA_RATE=0x103E; PLAYBACK_STATE=0x1035 / MEDIA_POSITION=0x1036 / MEDIA_VOLUME=0x1037 live on the controller
 
 ### Colors
 
 - Literal colors are **sRGB** with D65 white point, packed as `0xAARRGGBB`
 - A color property may instead carry a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference to a token path
 - Semantic token resolution and theme adaptation are **renderer-owned**
 
 ### Design Token System
 
 **Core Principle**: Application defines intent, overrides, and the theme.
 Renderer defines visual appearance, behavior, defaults, and interaction states.
 
 - The **application owns the theme**: token overrides (base = **light**, `dark.`-prefixed = **dark**) and token references in style properties. Token refs cover COLOR and non-color values (`Length` for spacing/padding/font size/radius/border/frame; `FontFamily.Token` for STRING) in the Rust and Kotlin DSLs.
 - The **renderer owns** default token values (light + dark, the full Tier-1 catalog), token resolution (including explicit `dark.` = forced dark and parent fallback), effective color-scheme detection, interaction states (hover, pressed, focus, disabled), and theme adaptation
 - `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` identifies tokens by **dot-separated string paths** (e.g. `color.primary`, `space.2`) with the standard value-type encoding — there is no separate numeric tokenId system. A `dark.` prefix selects the dark variant (`dark.color.primary`); a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference whose path starts with `dark.` forces the dark value in either scheme
 - **Runtime theming**: `META::RESET_THEME` clears every app override; a replacement theme is reset + `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides in one frame. `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` forces `platform`/`light`/`dark`. Both are renderer state — no node is re-emitted. Java: `Emitter.replaceTheme`/`setColorScheme` + `PathlandSession.setTheme`/`setColorScheme`; Rust: `Engine::reset_theme`/`set_color_scheme`.
 - An unresolvable token reference leaves the property **unset** (renderer default), never an error or stale value.
 - The protocol MUST NEVER describe hover styles, click styles, visual transitions, conditional styling, or layout tuning for interaction states
 - **Deferred**: applying per-component tokens to native GTK/Qt leaf control chrome; web parent-path fallback.
 
 The HTML renderer's default token values are generated from `design/` (see
 "HTML base design" above). Full details: [Design Token System](./spec/OPCODE.md#design-token-system)
 and the canonical catalog / color-scheme contract in [spec/TOKENS.md](./spec/TOKENS.md).

 ## Implementation Guidelines
 
 ### Adding New Component
 1. Add to `component_type` in `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/constants.rs`
 2. Document in `spec/OPCODE.md`
 3. Implement the component type in `pathland-core` (if it affects the retained tree)
 4. Implement native-element mapping in the target renderer (Goal 3–5)
 5. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Adding New Property
 1. Add to the appropriate property module in `constants.rs`
 2. Document in `spec/OPCODE.md`
 3. Handle the value type in `pathland-core`'s diff emission (if a stack/text/size property)
 4. Implement in each renderer's property application
 5. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Modifying Protocol
 1. Update `spec/OPCODE.md` first (and `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` vectors)
 2. Update `constants.rs` and `pathland-core` encoding/emitters
 3. Run `cd lib/rust && cargo run -p pathland-protocol-manifest` and commit the
    updated `spec/protocol.tsv`
 4. Update the hand-written JVM protocol constants (the Java manifest test fails
    with the exact missing/stale row otherwise)
 5. If emission behavior changed, run
    `cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --emit` and commit the trace fixtures
 6. Verify backward compatibility; update `pathland-core`/renderers + tests
 7. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Changing the Wire Format
 - Bump the wire `version` field in `spec/OPCODE.md` and `pathland-core`'s header (currently 1). Pre-release format changes are acceptable while version stays 1.
 
 ### Keeping implementation status updated (MANDATORY)
 
 **The agent MUST keep the per-project `status.md` files in sync with the code.**
 Whenever you land a protocol or renderer change — a new component/property/
 command/event, a new encoder/decoder, a new widget mapping, a new modifier or
 renderer feature, a test that proves new surface — **update the affected
 project's `status.md`** (Implemented / Not implemented / gaps) in the same
 change. The specs (`spec/`) describe the protocol contract only and MUST NOT
 carry implementation status; status lives in `status.md` next to each
 implementing project.
 
 ---
 
 ## Common Pitfalls
 
 ### NEVER Do These
 | Anti-Pattern | Why Wrong | Correct |
 |--------------|-----------|---------|
 | Renderer stores application state | Violates statelessness | Application owns the tree |
 | Engine computes layout / emits rects | Violates declarative model | Emit structure + constraints; native elements lay out |
 | Send full trees | Inefficient | Diff-based reactive emission |
 | String property names | Larger payloads | Use numeric IDs |
 | String component names | Larger payloads | Use numeric IDs |
 | Generic RGB | Ambiguous | Explicitly sRGB |
 | Hover styles in protocol | Renderer job | Define in theme |
 | Heap allocation in steady-state emission | Slow | Preallocated snapshot slab + arena |

 ## Pathland Mindset
 
 **Always remember**:
 1. Protocol is King
 2. Renderers are Dumb (execute commands only)
 3. Applications are Smart (generate commands)
 4. Only Changes Matter (transmit mutations / reactive emission)
 5. Binary is Beautiful (efficient, deterministic)
 
 **When in doubt**: Check `spec/OPCODE.md`, the conformance vectors in `spec/CONFORMANCE.md`, and the companion catalogs (`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`, `spec/MODIFIERS.md`, `spec/EVENTS.md`, `spec/LAYOUT.md`), and the reference implementation (`pathland-core`). Ask: "Does this maintain stateless renderers?" "Does this only transmit actual changes?" "Does this describe WHAT the UI is, never WHERE?" "Is this representable as a 16-byte opcode in any language?"

+# External UI updates with topic subscriptions
+
+Pathland signals are single-threaded by contract: reads, writes, and effects run
+on the session's actor. Background work (Kafka/SmallRye `@Incoming` consumers,
+scheduled jobs, database notifications, other transports) runs on its own
+threads, so it must not set a view's signal directly.
+
+Topic subscriptions are the supported bridge. A view subscribes to a
+**strongly typed, always-scoped** topic and gets a normal `Signal<T>`; external
+code publishes a value for the same `(topic, subject)` pair from any thread, and
+only the sessions subscribed to that pair update. The runtime applies the value
+on each session's actor, so the existing effect/delta path is unchanged.
+
+## 1. Declare the topic once
+
+A `Topic<T, S>` carries the payload type `T` and the subject type `S`. Topic
+identity is its name, so the view and the publisher share the same constant.
+
+```kotlin
+object CustomerTopics {
+    val NAME: Topic<String, Long> = Topic.of("customer.name")
+    val ORDERS: Topic<List<Order>, Long> = Topic.of("customer.orders")
+}
+```
+
+```java
+public final class CustomerTopics {
+    public static final Topic<String, Long> NAME = Topic.of("customer.name");
+    public static final Topic<List<Order>, Long> ORDERS = Topic.of("customer.orders");
+
+    private CustomerTopics() {}
+}
+```
+
+## 2. Subscribe in a view
+
+```kotlin
+class CustomerOrdersView(
+    private val customerId: Long,
+    private val initialName: String,
+    private val initialOrders: List<Order>,
+) : Component() {
+
+    private val name = topic(CustomerTopics.NAME, customerId, initialName)
+    private val orders = topic(CustomerTopics.ORDERS, customerId, initialOrders)
+
+    override fun body(): View = VStack(spacing = 8) {
+        Text(name)                          // Signal<String>
+        ForEach(orders) { OrderCard(it) }   // Signal<List<Order>>
+    }
+}
+```
+
+`topic(...)` returns a regular `Signal<T>`, so `Text(signal)`,
+`ForEach(signal)`, `signal.map { }`, and `computed { }` all work. Subscribing is
+idempotent per `(topic, subject)` within a session; repeated calls return the
+same local signal.
+
+Passing the wrong subject or payload type is a compile error: `NAME` requires a
+`Long` subject and a `String` value.
+
+## 3. Publish from any thread
+
+The starter produces a `PathlandSignalHub` bean for the root mount (use
+`PathlandHost.signalHub(mount)` in a multi-app host). Publishing is
+non-blocking.
+
+```java
+@ApplicationScoped
+public class CustomerConsumers {
+
+    @Inject PathlandSignalHub hub;
+
+    @Incoming("customer-name-changed")
+    void onNameChanged(CustomerNameChanged event) {
+        hub.publish(CustomerTopics.NAME, event.customerId(), event.name());
+    }
+}
+```
+
+Only sessions that subscribed to `(customer.name, event.customerId())` are
+updated. Two customers, two sessions: publishing customer 42's name never
+touches customer 43.
+
+## Semantics
+
+- **Scoped, not broadcast.** The hub looks up subscribers by
+  `(topic.name, subject)`. There is no global publish path.
+- **Actor-confined.** Published values are applied on the session actor, so all
+  signal reads/writes/effects keep the single-threaded contract.
+- **Latest wins.** Publishes are coalesced per session: at most one drain task is
+  scheduled, and only the newest value per subscription is applied. A hot
+  producer cannot flood the actor.
+- **`initial` seeds the signal.** A new session renders current data from its own
+  source; subsequent changes arrive through `publish`. Late subscribers do not
+  receive historical values.
+- **Session-scoped lifetime.** Subscriptions end when the session closes.
+  `SessionContext.current()?.unsubscribe(topic, subject)` is available for dynamic
+  subjects; SSR sessions subscribe for the first paint but do not register with
+  the hub.
+- **Multi-app isolation.** Each mounted app has its own hub; `/` and `/billing`
+  never see each other's topics.
+
+## Notes
+
+- Declare a topic once and share the constant. The topic name is the wire
+  identity (a future Redis fan-out can route on it); two topics with the same
+  name must carry the same types.
+- The subject should be immutable with stable `equals`/`hashCode` — an id, a
+  value class, or a record.
+- For an app-wide stream, use an explicit singleton subject
+  (`object GlobalSubject`) as the `S` type; every subscription is still scoped.
+- If you need a lower-level escape hatch, `PathlandSession.submit(Runnable)` and
+  `SessionContext.current()?.submit { }` run work on the session actor.

 # pathland-quarkus — implementation status
 
-**Last updated:** November 6, 2026
+**Last updated:** November 7, 2026
 
 Quarkus extension for Pathland: SSR at any path, live deltas over each
 app's reserved `/{base}/ws`, per-session state. Adding this extension + a
 `PathlandApp` CDI bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at
 their own subpaths (the BFF layout). Author the root view with
 `pathland-view-core`'s Kotlin DSL; Java hosts return Kotlin views from a
 `PathlandApp` bean. The extension also provides the `dev.pathland.quarkus.kotlin`
 capability and pulls in `quarkus-kotlin`.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Security defaults (issue #63)**: the deployment module contributes
   overridable runtime defaults via `RunTimeConfigurationDefaultBuildItem`:
   `quarkus.http.cors.enabled=true` (no origins → same-origin, which covers
   WebSocket upgrades because the CORS filter runs before routes),
   `quarkus.websockets-next.server.max-message-size`/`max-frame-size=65536`, and
   CSP + `X-Content-Type-Options`/`Referrer-Policy`/`X-Frame-Options` headers via
   `quarkus.http.header.*`. See `docs/HARDENING.md` for overrides, CSP rollout,
   reverse-proxy/TLS guidance, and edge rate limiting. The `wid` handshake query
   is validated by server-core (`WindowIds`). **HSTS is deliberately not an
   extension default** — it is a whole-origin, persistent browser policy that
   also covers other apps on the same server, so it is owned by the application
   or edge; the Quarkus demo opts in via `application.properties`.
   `docs/HARDENING.md` documents the directives and override guidance.
 - **Hosted deployments work by default**: the same defaults set
   `quarkus.http.proxy.proxy-address-forwarding`, `allow-x-forwarded`, and
   `enable-forwarded-host` to `true`, so a TLS-terminating PaaS (Render, Fly,
   Heroku, Cloud Run) gets a correct same-origin WebSocket check and an external
   SSR canonical URL with zero configuration. These are lowest-priority defaults;
   application config (including
   `quarkus.http.proxy.proxy-address-forwarding=false`) always wins.
+- **Topic hub bean**: the extension produces a `PathlandSignalHub` singleton
+  (`host.signalHub()`: root mount, else the first mount) for external UI updates.
+  `TopicSubscriptionsTest` mounts a `/topics` app and proves a background-thread
+  publish reaches only the session subscribed for that subject.
 - **Java host / Kotlin views**: `CounterApp` is a Java CDI bean whose
   `newRoot()` returns a Kotlin-authored fixture view; the multi-session
   WebSocket tests prove SSR + live deltas work through that mount.
 
 - **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt.
 - **SEO document head (issue #45)**: `IndexResource` derives the canonical URL
   from `UriInfo` and passes host-default `PageMetadata` to the registry;
   `PathlandApp.pageMetadata(...)` may override it per route before the first
   paint. Canonical/OG/Twitter/JSON-LD are on by default and configurable via
   `pathland.seo.{enabled,site-name,image,og-type,twitter-card,twitter-site,structured-data}`.
 
 - **`PathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/_pathland/ws")` for the root app: 1:1 sessions
   per connection (a fresh `uiId` per connection + the client's `wid` state scope from
   the `?wid=` query param), binary events routed into the root registry of the
   `PathlandHost`. **Stateless (critical)**: quarkus-websockets-next endpoints default
   to `@Singleton` — one shared instance for all connections — so the per-connection
   ids come from `connection.id()` + the handshake and the `QuarkusConnection` adapters
   live in a map keyed by connection id. Memoizing `uiId`/`wid`/`transport` on the
   shared instance collapsed every connection onto ONE session (multiple browsers shared
   one UI model — a probe or second tab drove the first tab's session).
 - **`MountedPathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/{app}/_pathland/ws")` for mounted apps:
   the `{app}` path param resolves the app's registry. Mount paths are single-segment.
   Same stateless rule as the root socket.
 - **`IndexResource`** — JAX-RS SSR catch-all (`/` + deep links; `/_pathland/**` and the
   Quarkus non-application root `/q/**` — health/metrics — excluded via negative lookahead)
   dispatching to the longest-mount app (prefix stripped);
   SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS);
   per-app framework files (`/{app}/_pathland/...`, e.g. the mounted app's bundle) are
   served from the shared `/_pathland/**` classpath mount. Quarkus serves the global
   `/_pathland/**` bundle + asset mount from `META-INF/resources` before JAX-RS.
   **`/_pathland/{name}.css`** (global JAX-RS route + the mounted-base
   `frameworkFile` path) serves the renderer-owned content-hashed base design
   (`HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` at `baseCssName()`) as `text/css` with
   `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. **`/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg`**
   serves the renderer-owned icon glyphs from the shared Rust renderer
   (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` → `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an `immutable` cache
   header — no static CSS/icon files on any host. SSR links the CSS via
   `PathlandSession` → `renderLinked`.
 - **`PathlandRegistryProducer`** — CDI `@Produces @Singleton` `PathlandHost` from every
   `MountedApp` bean plus the lone `PathlandApp` bean (mounted at `/`); `@Disposes` shuts
   it down. Reads the `pathland.debug-html` config property (default `false`) to enable
   per-node HTML comments in SSR output, and `pathland.service-worker` (default `false`)
   to opt the DOM client into the per-window-id service worker (issue #155) — served at
   `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`.
 - **`ServiceWorkerFilter`** — serves `/_pathland/sw.js` (root and mounted bases) with
   `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`, so the client's root-scoped
   registration succeeds. A `Filters` handler always runs before routes, so it wins over
   Quarkus's static-resource handler (which sends neither header, and whose configured
   max-age would otherwise cache the script and delay update detection). The script is
   resolved through the thread-context classloader first, then the extension's own
   loader, then the system loader: extension runtime classes live in Quarkus's base
   runtime classloader and cannot see the application's `META-INF/resources` copy. The
   extension jar bundles the worker as a fallback (the TS copy script writes it), and
   `pathland-quarkus-demo`'s integration test asserts the headers on both the root and a
   mounted base — the packaged-app classloader path the module-local test could not see.
 - **Observability (issue #62)** — `quarkus-micrometer` (a `MeterRegistry` bean) +
   `quarkus-smallrye-health`: the producer builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over the
   registry and decorates it with `TracingTelemetry` when a `Tracer` bean is present and
   `quarkus.otel.enabled` (default `true`; the extension never touches the OTel API when
   the extension is absent/disabled). `PathlandHealthCheck` (`@Readiness`) reports the
   host UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/q/health`; the `pathland.*` meters appear
   at `/q/metrics`.
 - **`QuarkusConnection`** — adapts `WebSocketConnection` to `PathlandConnection`.
   Sends are **serialized** (one `sendBinary` subscription in flight, the rest queued),
   and a **send failure closes the connection** so the session drops it and the DOM
   client reconnects + `META::RESYNC` (recoverable) instead of silently stalling on an
   "open" socket that never delivers (the remote seekbar symptom). **Send timeout**: a
   `sendBinary` that neither completes nor fails within 10 s (a half-dead connection /
   a dropped proxy upstream leg) is marked failed and closed — a hung send would
   otherwise wedge the serialized drain forever. **Keep-alive pings**: the connection
   sends a WS-protocol ping every 15 s (browsers auto-pong) to keep the connection warm
   through middleboxes and detect a dead client; `close()` stops the keep-alive
   scheduler (the sockets' `@OnClose` calls it).
 - **Heartbeat** — both sockets reply to a client `META::PING` with a `META::PONG`
   **at the transport layer** (through their `QuarkusConnection`, no actor/session
   dependency, and a PING never creates or wakes a session); spec/OPCODE.md
   §Transport heartbeat.
 - **Failure handling** — `fail()` logs the reason; `close()` (socket `@OnClose`)
   no longer calls `close()` on the already-closed connection (no spurious
   "Connection already closed" noise). A **transient write failure on a connection
   that still reports open is logged, not closed** — only a confirmed-dead channel
   (or a send hung past the timeout) warrants closing. The send-timeout task is
   **cancelled when the send completes**, so a completed-but-late callback can't
   false-time-out and kill a healthy connection. Keep-alive pings are sent directly
   (Vert.x serializes writes — no sync with `sendBinary` needed).
 - `META-INF/beans.xml` so Quarkus discovers the extension.
 - **Quarkus extension metadata** — runtime + `pathland-quarkus-deployment`; the
   runtime provides the `dev.pathland.quarkus` capability. The runtime has no
   dependency on the authoring DSL. Tests use Kotlin-authored fixture views to prove
   a Java CDI bean can mount them.
 
 ## App DX
 
 ```java
 @ApplicationScoped
 public class MyApp {
     @Produces @Singleton PathlandApp main() { return () -> new MyHomeView(); }
     @Produces @Singleton MountedApp support() { return MountedApp.of("/support", ...); }
 }
 ```
 
 ## Verified by
 
 Manual: the `pathland-quarkus-demo` renders `/` (the music player, whose Now
 Playing pane embeds the small `/ad` app via a **same-server `ProxyView`**,
 spec/PROXY.md) and `/ad` (the ad app); a WebSocket handshake to `/_pathland/ws`
 and `/ad/_pathland/ws` returns 101. `ProxyDemoTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts
 `GET /` embeds the `/ad` app's subtree with remapped node ids
 (`data-pathland-id="1073741825"` — proxy block 0 + origin id 1). Core behavior is
 covered by `pathland-server-core` tests. `MultiSessionWebSocketTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) opens **100 concurrent real WS
 sessions** against `/_pathland/ws` (via the shared `pathland-server-core` test-jar
 probe) and asserts each connects, re-syncs, gets transport-level PONGs, stays isolated,
 and is never closed by the peer.
 `PathlandObservabilityTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts `/q/health` reports the Pathland
 check UP and `/q/metrics` exposes the `pathland.*` namespace. `BaseCssTest`
 (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts the linked SSR `<link>`, the immutable `text/css`
 response at the global and mounted bases, and a 404 for an unknown hash.

+package dev.pathland.server
+
+import dev.pathland.view.core.Environment
+import dev.pathland.view.core.Platform
+import dev.pathland.view.core.View
+import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Opcode
+import dev.pathland.view.core.signal.Signal
+import dev.pathland.view.core.signal.Signals
+import dev.pathland.view.core.state.InMemoryStateStore
+import dev.pathland.view.core.subscription.Topic
+import dev.pathland.view.core.transport.EnvironmentData
+import dev.pathland.view.core.transport.FrameCodec
+import dev.pathland.view.core.transport.ProtocolFrame
+import dev.pathland.view.dsl.Component
+import dev.pathland.view.dsl.Text
+import dev.pathland.view.dsl.topic
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test
+import java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList
+import java.util.function.Consumer
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertFalse
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertThrows
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue
+
+/**
+ * Topic subscriptions: strongly typed `(topic, subject)` routing, actor-confined
+ * application, coalescing, and close/unsubscribe cleanup.
+ */
+class TopicsTest {
+
+    private val name: Topic<String, Long> = Topic.of("test.customer.name")
+
+    @Test
+    fun publishTargetsOnlyTheSubscribedSubject() {
+        val registry = registry(::probe)
+        val customer42 = RecordingConnection()
+        val customer43 = RecordingConnection()
+        open(registry, "u42", "w42", "/42", customer42)
+        open(registry, "u43", "w43", "/43", customer43)
+        await { customer42.has("initial-42") && customer43.has("initial-43") }
+
+        registry.signalHub().publish(name, 42L, "Alice")
+
+        await { customer42.has("Alice") }
+        Thread.sleep(100)
+        assertFalse(customer43.has("Alice"), "customer 43 must not receive customer 42's update")
+        assertTrue(customer43.has("initial-43"))
+        assertEquals(1, registry.signalHub().subscriberCount(name, 42L))
+        assertEquals(1, registry.signalHub().subscriberCount(name, 43L))
+        registry.shutdown()
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun everySessionForTheSameSubjectUpdates() {
+        val registry = registry(::probe)
+        val first = RecordingConnection()
+        val second = RecordingConnection()
+        open(registry, "a", "wa", "/42", first)
+        open(registry, "b", "wb", "/42", second)
+        await { first.has("initial-42") && second.has("initial-42") }
+
+        registry.signalHub().publish(name, 42L, "Alice")
+
+        await { first.has("Alice") && second.has("Alice") }
+        assertEquals(2, registry.signalHub().subscriberCount(name, 42L))
+        registry.shutdown()
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun rapidPublishesCoalesceToTheLatestValue() {
+        val registry = registry(::probe)
+        val conn = RecordingConnection()
+        open(registry, "u42", "w42", "/42", conn)
+        await { conn.has("initial-42") }
+
+        for (i in 1..200) {
+            registry.signalHub().publish(name, 42L, "v$i")
+        }
+
+        await { conn.has("v200") }
+        val applied = conn.texts().filter { it.startsWith("v") }.map { it.removePrefix("v").toInt() }
+        assertTrue(applied.zipWithNext().all { (a, b) -> a <= b }, "values never go backwards: $applied")
+        assertFalse(applied.any { it > 200 })
+        registry.shutdown()
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun updatesAreAppliedOnTheSessionActor() {
+        val threads = CopyOnWriteArrayList<String>()
+        val registry = registry { subjectProbe { threads.add(Thread.currentThread().name) } }
+        val conn = RecordingConnection()
+        open(registry, "u42", "w42", "/42", conn)
+        await { conn.has("initial-42") }
+
+        registry.signalHub().publish(name, 42L, "Alice")
+        await { conn.has("Alice") }
+
+        assertTrue(threads.isNotEmpty())
+        assertTrue(
+            threads.all { it.startsWith("pathland-actor") },
+            "all renders must run on the session actor, saw $threads",
+        )
+        registry.shutdown()
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun closingASessionRemovesItsSubscriptions() {
+        val registry = registry(::probe)
+        val conn = RecordingConnection()
+        open(registry, "u42", "w42", "/42", conn)
+        await { conn.has("initial-42") }
+        assertEquals(1, registry.signalHub().subscriberCount(name, 42L))
+
+        registry.close("u42")
+        await { registry.signalHub().subscriberCount(name, 42L) == 0 }
+
+        registry.signalHub().publish(name, 42L, "after-close")
+        Thread.sleep(50)
+        assertFalse(conn.has("after-close"))
+        registry.shutdown()
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun unsubscribeStopsRoutingAndKeepsTheLastValue() {
+        val hub = PathlandSignalHub("/", PathlandTelemetry.NOOP)
+        val subscriptions = SessionSubscriptions(
+            hub,
+            Consumer { it.run() },
+            PathlandTelemetry.NOOP,
+            "/",
+        )
+        val signal: Signal<String> = subscriptions.subscribe(name, 42L, "initial")
+        assertEquals(1, hub.subscriberCount(name, 42L))
+
+        hub.publish(name, 42L, "Alice")
+        assertEquals("Alice", signal.get())
+
+        subscriptions.unsubscribe(name, 42L)
+        assertEquals(0, hub.subscriberCount(name, 42L))
+        hub.publish(name, 42L, "ignored")
+        assertEquals("Alice", signal.get())
+        subscriptions.close()
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun fieldDeclaredSubscriptionResolvesDuringMount() {
+        val registry = registry {
+            object : Component() {
+                private val nameSignal = topic(name, 42L, "field-42")
+
+                override fun body(): View = Text(nameSignal)
+            }
+        }
+        val conn = RecordingConnection()
+        open(registry, "u42", "w42", "/42", conn)
+        await { conn.has("field-42") }
+
+        registry.signalHub().publish(name, 42L, "Alice")
+        await { conn.has("Alice") }
+        registry.shutdown()
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun topicOutsideASessionResolvesLazilyAndFailsOnRead() {
+        val signal = Signals.topic(name, 42L, "initial")
+        assertThrows(IllegalStateException::class.java) { signal.get() }
+    }
+
+    private fun registry(app: () -> View): PathlandRegistry =
+        PathlandRegistry({ app() }, InMemoryStateStore())
+
+    private fun open(
+        registry: PathlandRegistry,
+        uiId: String,
+        windowId: String,
+        route: String,
+        connection: RecordingConnection,
+    ) {
+        registry.open(uiId, windowId, connection)
+        registry.environment(uiId, EnvironmentData.of(route))
+        registry.resync(uiId)
+    }
+
+    /** A text view bound to `test.customer.name` for the customer id in the route. */
+    private fun probe(): View = subjectProbe()
+
+    private fun subjectProbe(onRender: () -> Unit = {}): View = object : Component() {
+        override fun body(): View {
+            val id = subject()
+            val nameSignal = topic(name, id, "initial-$id")
+            onRender()
+            return Text(nameSignal)
+        }
+    }
+
+    private fun Component.subject(): Long =
+        Environment.value(Platform.ACTIVE_PATH).get().trim('/').toLongOrNull() ?: 0L
+
+    private fun await(timeoutMillis: Long = 10_000, condition: () -> Boolean) {
+        val deadline = System.nanoTime() + timeoutMillis * 1_000_000
+        while (!condition() && System.nanoTime() < deadline) {
+            Thread.sleep(5)
+        }
+        assertTrue(condition(), "condition not met within ${timeoutMillis}ms")
+    }
+
+    /** A connection that records decoded SET_TEXT values. */
+    private class RecordingConnection : PathlandConnection {
+        private val recorded = CopyOnWriteArrayList<ByteArray>()
+
+        override fun send(bytes: ByteArray) {
+            recorded.add(bytes)
+        }
+
+        override fun isOpen(): Boolean = true
+
+        fun texts(): List<String> {
+            val values = ArrayList<String>()
+            for (bytes in recorded) {
+                val frame: ProtocolFrame = try {
+                    FrameCodec.decodeFrame(bytes)
+                } catch (_: RuntimeException) {
+                    continue
+                }
+                for (op: Opcode in frame.opcodes()) {
+                    if (op.category() == 0x02 && op.command() == 0x03) { // PARAMETER::SET_TEXT
+                        values.add(frame.stringAt(op.b()))
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+            return values
+        }
+
+        fun has(text: String): Boolean = texts().contains(text)
+    }
+}

No web-framework dependency — framework glue lives in the starters. ## Implemented - **Security hardening (issue #63)**: `WindowIds` validates the client-supplied `wid` (≤128 chars, `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`; a colon is rejected so it cannot collide with the mount-qualified state scope). Invalid ids are treated as absent (SSR defaults) or replaced with a fresh UUID on the WebSocket. `InboundRateLimiter` bounds inbound batches/bytes per connection before actor work is queued (`pathland.max-inbound-batches-per-second`, default 500; `pathland.max-inbound-bytes-per-second`, default 2 MiB) and reports drops via `PathlandTelemetry.inboundDropped` (`pathland.inbound.dropped`). The SSR script tag now carries `integrity="sha384-…"` from the manifest's second line (`PathlandAssets.bundleIntegrity()`); an older one-line manifest simply omits it. - **Attributed text transport**: `FrameRebase` rebases `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`'s string-section offset (like `SET_TEXT`) for delta batching/frame merging, and `ProxyIdMap` remaps its node id. - **Window metadata + SSR head attrs**: `PathlandSession.renderHtml` injects host attrs into the renderer's opening `` (which now carries `lang`), and `FrameRebase` rebases `SET_WINDOW_METADATA` string offsets. Proxy origin metadata is dropped with the other META opcodes. - **Per-route SEO metadata (issue #45)**: `PageMetadata`/`PageMetadataRequest` carry canonical URL, Open Graph/Twitter cards, and JSON-LD. `PathlandApp` gains a default `pageMetadata(request)` hook (active mount-stripped route + host canonical URL); `PathlandRegistry.renderHtml(route, wid, hostDefaults)` merges host defaults with the app's per-route overrides before SSR. Existing overloads keep the legacy head. - **`PathlandApp`** — the app's root-view factory (`View newRoot()` + optional `theme()`); the single app-specific piece a starter needs. - **`MountedApp`** — `record MountedApp(String path, PathlandApp app)`: one app mounted at a subpath prefix (normalized; `/` = root). Hosts any number of them. - **`PathlandHost`** — the multi-app dispatcher: one `PathlandRegistry` per mounted app (own actor thread, own sessions). `match(requestUri)` resolves the owning registry by **longest mount-prefix match** and reports the **mount-stripped route** (a root mount claims every unclaimed path). Duplicate mount paths are rejected at construction. - **`PathlandRegistry`** — session lifecycle per app: single actor thread, 1:1 sessions keyed by a **per-connection `uiId`** (a fresh id per WebSocket connection, so two windows of the same browser never share a UI model), lazy creation on first environment message, pending connections (each carrying the mount-prefixed state scope from the client's per-window `wid`), `open(uiId, wid, conn)`/`environment`/`dispatch`/`resync`/`close`/`renderHtml`/`shutdown`. New: - `mountPath()`/`base()` — each app's framework base is `//_pathland` (`/_pathland` for the root), emitted as `data-pathland-base` in SSR; - `stateScope(windowId)` — app-qualified state-store scope (`mount:wid`) so apps and windows sharing a store never collide; - `stripRoute(route)` — strips the mount prefix from SSR routes, WS environment ROUTE fields, **and inbound `NAVIGATE` URLs** (browser back/forward sends the real address, e.g. `http://host/app2/home`), so a mounted app always sees its own route space (`/app2/home` → `/home`). `Router.pathOf` is reused for URL→path extraction. - `shutdown()` — serialized on the actor and idempotent: work enqueued after shutdown starts is dropped, sessions are closed on the actor thread, then the executor is stopped and awaited. Teardown can no longer race a queued mount/resync mutating the same emitter (regression-tested by `shutdownSerializesWithQueuedActorWork`). +- **Topic subscriptions / external UI updates**: `PathlandSignalHub` (one per mount) + routes `publish(topic, subject, value)` only to sessions subscribed to that exact + `(topic, subject)` pair; `SessionSubscriptions` holds each session's local mirror, + coalesces publishes latest-wins, schedules one actor drain, and unregisters on + close/unsubscribe. `PathlandSession.submit(Runnable)` hands arbitrary work to the + session actor from any thread; a session context is installed around every actor + task (mount, dispatch, drain, theming) so `topic(...)` resolves during render. + `PathlandHost.signalHub()`/`signalHub(mount)` expose the hub. Telemetry: + `topics.published`/`coalesced`/`dropped`. See `docs/external-updates.md` and + `TopicsTest`. - **Per-window isolation (no session cookie)**: session identity (the `uiId` map key) is deliberately separate from the persisted-state scope (the client's `wid`, carried only on the WebSocket URL — never in the page URL, so the address bar stays clean). The SSR request therefore has no `wid`: `renderHtml(route, wid)` with a null `wid` renders defaults; the client's live session is scoped by the WS `wid`, and a same-tab reload re-syncs that window's persisted state over the WebSocket. The old `session` cookie is removed. - **`PathlandSession`** — per-session: builds the `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` signal, mounts `app.newRoot().modifiers(environmentBinding(e -> e.key(ACTIVE_PATH).value(activePath)))`, **delta-batched send-on-`endFrame`** (`DeltaBatcher` coalesces per-signal frames into one batch — flush ~20 ms or 16 KB, string offsets rebased — so a continuous input burst can't overflow a remote WebSocket send queue), `applyEnvironment` (re-route guard-aware via the bound router), `dispatch` (tap/nav-intent/text/value/date/NAVIGATE), `resync`, `renderHtml`, `close`. Runtime theming: `setTheme(ThemeData)`, `resetTheme()`, and `setColorScheme(ThemeMode)` emit one `META::RESET_THEME` + `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` frame or `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` to the live client (renderer state; no tree re-emission). The SSR document keeps the mount theme until a resync/reload. `sendBatch` drops the connection on any send failure (a client reconnect then re-syncs via `META::RESYNC` instead of silently stalling on an "open" socket); `closeConnection` best-effort closes an `AutoCloseable` adapter (the starters now close their underlying WebSocket on failure). Now takes the app's `base` and `stateScope` explicitly (the registry supplies them). - **`DeltaBatcher`** — merges session delta frames (opcodes + a single rebased string section) and flushes as one network batch on a timer/byte threshold; the Java analogue of the Rust transport's `Batcher`. It owns the per-session **message sequence** (stamped on each flushed batch via `FrameCodec.encodeFrame(frame, sequence)`) so the DOM client can detect a lost batch and recover with `META::RESYNC` (spec/OPCODE.md §Sequence gap detection); an empty flush consumes no sequence. The **sender runs OUTSIDE the monitor** — a blocking/queueing send can never stall the actor thread's `append` or the flush scheduler. Coalescing tests cover merging + rebasing, a 100-frame burst collapsing to one send, incrementing sequences, and a blocking sender not holding the lock. - **`PathlandConnection`** — the transport seam (`send(byte[])`/`isOpen()`); each starter adapts its WebSocket type to it. - **Observability seam** — `PathlandTelemetry` (default `NOOP`): the runtime emits session open/close, inbound event batches, inbound drops (oversize/rate), flushed batches (frames/opcodes/bytes + merge-encode time), SSR render latency, resync requests, and send failures; the host binds a pull-based active-sessions gauge. `PathlandHost`/`PathlandRegistry`/ `PathlandSession`/`DeltaBatcher` thread it through (a host with no telemetry pays nothing). This module also ships the `dev.pathland.observability` Micrometer + OpenTelemetry adapters; the starters auto-wire them. Logging is **SLF4J** (both frameworks bind it) — the old ad-hoc `System.out` is gone. See issue #62. - **Concurrency stress** — `RegistryConcurrencyTest`: 100 sessions driven through the registry concurrently (clicks on each session's button) while SSR-style requests construct throwaway sessions on request threads — the shared-actor / global-`Scheduler` cross-session corruption guard. Each session must reach exactly its own click count (no lost effects, no cross-session values). - **Shared WS test harness** — `dev.pathland.server.test.{WsSession,MultiSessionProbe}` (a JDK-WebSocket client speaking the PLPL protocol: env/resync/click/ping) lives in this module in main scope, so package builds resolve it as a normal jar; the starters' 100-session stress tests reuse it. - **`StateStores`** — default state store: Redis when reachable, else the supplied fallback. The `dev.pathland.state.redis.RedisStateStore` (Lettuce) ships in this module too. - **Observability adapters** — `dev.pathland.observability.MicrometerTelemetry` turns the seam into `pathland.*` meters (counters, timers, a distribution summary, a pull-based sessions gauge, every meter tagged by `mount`); the optional `TracingTelemetry` decorator emits an OpenTelemetry span per frame send / inbound event batch / SSR render. Micrometer is a compile dependency; the OTel API is `optional`, so a host that does not enable tracing pays nothing. - **SSR debug comments (property-gated)**: `PathlandSession`/`PathlandRegistry` take a `debugHtml` flag (constructor + `isDebugHtml()`); when set, `renderHtml` uses the renderer's debug mode so every rendered node is prefixed with an HTML comment naming its component and the modifiers applied. The Spring/Quarkus starters bind it to the `pathland.debug-html` property (default `false`). - **Reserved framework root**: `PathlandSession.PATHLAND_BASE` (`/_pathland`) — the SSR page carries the app's base as `data-pathland-base` and the DOM-client bundle is injected at `{base}/dom-renderer-.js` (`PathlandAssets` reads the current name from the `_pathland/dom-renderer.current` manifest on the classpath, resolving through the thread context classloader first so a Quarkus extension parent loader can see the application's static resources; it falls back to the literal `dom-renderer.js` only when absent) so the client's WebSocket and asset refs resolve from the same reserved prefix (spec DSL.md). The content-hashed name busts the immutable asset cache with a fresh URL per build. The built-in base design is linked the same way: `renderHtml` renders through `HtmlRenderer.renderLinked(frame, root, base)`, so the CSS href is `{base}/base-.css` (token overrides/fit rules stay inline). Multi-app hosts give each mount its own base. - **Per-window-id service worker (opt-in, issue #155)**: `PathlandHost` carries a host-level `serviceWorker` flag (default `false`; one registration covers the whole origin) threaded to every `PathlandRegistry`; `PathlandSession.renderHtml` emits `data-pathland-service-worker="true"` on `` when set, and the DOM client registers `{base}/sw.js` (root scope) / unregisters when absent (the kill switch). `PathlandRegistry.serviceWorkerUrl()` names the served script. `renderHtml` also emits `data-pathland-ssr-scoped="true"` when the request carried a real per-window id, so the client can skip its initial `META::RESYNC` (the SSR was already rendered with that window's state and the live session shares it). ## Not implemented / gaps - No multi-node/shared sessions (each server owns its sessions in-memory). +- Topic fan-out is node-local: `PathlandSignalHub` routes to this process's + sessions only. A Redis/pub-sub-backed hub (each node fanning out to its local + sessions) is a follow-up; the topic name + subject are the stable wire keys. - Quarkus mounted-app WebSocket endpoints require a **single-segment** mount path (the `/{app}` path param); Spring supports any depth. ## Proxy views (spec/PROXY.md) — M1 (live) - **`proxy.ProxyIdMap`** — node-id namespacing: the reserved high range `[0x4000_0000, 0x8000_0000)`, 1024 blocks of `2^20`, the block math, and the opcode remap in both directions (`TREE` node ids + the node-id-bearing `PARAMETER` ops `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DATE` on ingress; `EVENT` targets on egress; `META` untouched). `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` is **not** remapped — its `A` is a token-path arena offset, not a node id (remapping it produced a huge out-of-bounds string offset → the client's RESYNC loop; regression-tested). Pure + unit-tested. - **`proxy.ProxyTransport`** + **`proxy.JdkWebSocketTransport`** — the outbound connection seam (default: the JDK `HttpClient` WebSocket client, no new dependency) with a `Factory` so a starter can swap a native client. - **`proxy.ProxySession`** — one origin connection: sends `META::ENVIRONMENT` + `META::RESYNC`, **remaps** the origin snapshot into the proxy's block and attaches the origin root under the proxy node, forwards live deltas remapped, routes client events back (target unmapped), replies `PONG` to origin `PING`, translates origin `META::RESET` into a **scoped** subtree teardown (never a global reset), tears the subtree down on disconnect (the origin session is per-connection), and reconnects with exponential backoff. While an SSR snapshot is pending, `awaitSnapshot` retries `META::RESYNC` every 500 ms, so a lost first handshake cannot consume the whole SSR budget. The service credential + a cycle-guard instance id ride the handshake headers. **Backpressure** (spec/PROXY.md §8): a "chatty origin" breaker (a per-second batch cap → drop + `RESYNC`) and event coalescing (pointer-moves coalesce by target; discrete events flush immediately). - **`proxy.ProxyHost`** — one `ProxySession` per `PROXY_VIEW` node, each with its own block; routes inbound events whose target is in a proxy range to the owning origin connection; owns the proxy scheduler. `reconcile(wanted)` starts a session for every `PROXY_VIEW` node and closes the session of every node that left the tree; released id blocks go to a **free-block pool** and are reused, so repeated removal/re-add cycles never exhaust the 1024-block range. - **`PathlandSession`** integration — captures `RenderResult.proxyViews()` and registers the emitter's structural-reconcile callback (`Emitter.onStructureReconciled`) to `reconcileProxies()`, so a proxy lives **exactly while its node is in the retained tree** (spec/PROXY.md §7): a `SizeThatFits` slot dropping the candidate that held it closes the origin connection, and re-adding it opens a fresh one (re-seeded by `META::RESYNC`). The host's frames feed the session's `DeltaBatcher` (a single unified sequence); `dispatch` splits proxy-range events to the origin and everything else to the app's own bindings; `close` tears the proxies down. `proxyTransportFactory(...)` lets a host supply a framework transport. - **`PathlandTelemetry`** — `proxyConnected`/`proxyDisconnected`/`proxyBatchDropped`/ `proxyResyncRequested` (all default no-ops). **SSR embed (M2).** `renderHtml` starts the proxies and **blocks** for each origin's snapshot (`ProxySession.awaitSnapshot`, bounded by a 2s timeout), then splices the remapped origin frames into the session's mount frame (`FrameMerger`, reusing the batcher's string rebasing via `FrameRebase`) so the renderer emits **one** document — the origin subtree plus its fit band rules in the same head. The origin's **global** token overrides (`SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`) are **dropped** (live + SSR): a proxied app renders under the **host's** theme, while its token *references* resolve against that theme (spec/PROXY.md §9). A proxy whose origin does not answer in time renders empty (a placeholder) and hydrates over the live connection. A client `META::RESYNC` also replays A's tree **and** asks every origin for a fresh snapshot (`ProxyHost.resyncAll`). **Gaps (M3):** nested proxies and per-proxy theme scoping are deferred (the origin's global overrides are dropped, not scoped, spec/PROXY.md §9). A tiny orphan window remains on removal: an origin batch already queued in the `DeltaBatcher` (≤20 ms) when the proxy node is removed can still create an unattached element in the client's `byId` (not in the DOM); eliminating it needs the `ProxySession` to track the ids it emitted and `DELETE` them on close. ## Verified by `mvn test` — `PathlandSessionTest`: mounts + routes taps through the binding maps, `applyEnvironment`/`resync`/`close` idempotent, registry SSR + lifecycle/teardown, **two windows with the same `wid` still get separate sessions** (a tap to one never reaches the other), and **message-before-open ordering** (environment/resync that race `open` still attach the connection and emit the snapshot). +`TopicsTest`: strongly typed `(topic, subject)` routing (customer 43 never sees +customer 42's update), every session for a subject updates, rapid publishes +coalesce latest-wins, updates run on the session actor, close removes +subscriptions, unsubscribe keeps the last value, and a topic outside a session +fails on read. `PathlandHostTest`: longest-prefix dispatch + route stripping, mount-boundary respect, no-root-mount 404, per-app base + state scope, duplicate-mount rejection, normalization, SSR emits the mounted app's base. `PathlandTelemetryTest`: a recording telemetry double asserts the registry emits session/event/resync/flush/SSR/close events, the host binds the active-sessions gauge, a failed send reports `connectionFailed`, and `DeltaBatcher` reports the flushed batch. `proxy.ProxyIdMapTest`: the reserved range, block round-trips, overflow rejection, and the opcode remap (TREE/PARAMETER node ids remapped, APPEND/META untouched, EVENT targets unmapped). `proxy.ProxySessionTest` (a fake origin transport): the ENVIRONMENT+RESYNC handshake + handshake headers, snapshot retry when the first RESYNC is lost, snapshot remap + root attachment, delta remap with the string section passed through verbatim, event egress unmapped, pointer-move coalescing, `META::RESET` → scoped teardown, disconnect teardown, and the chatty-origin drop+resync breaker. `proxy.ProxyIntegrationTest`: a `ProxyView` in the app tree opens an origin connection on `connect`, the remapped origin snapshot reaches the client (with the root attached), a client event in the proxy range routes back to the origin unmapped, and the SSR document embeds the origin subtree (remapped ids) in one render. `FrameMergerTest`: splicing a proxy's origin frame into an SSR frame rebases its string offsets (SET_TEXT / LIST / STRING operands) and returns the base  # pathland-spring-boot-starter — implementation status
 
-**Last updated:** November 6, 2026
+**Last updated:** November 7, 2026
 
 Spring Boot auto-configuration for Pathland: SSR at any path, live deltas over each
 app's reserved `/{base}/ws`, per-session state. Adding the starter dependency + a
 `PathlandApp` bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at their own
 subpaths (the BFF layout).
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Security hardening (issue #63)**: the WebSocket handlers no longer hardcode
   `setAllowedOrigins("*")`. The default is Spring's same-origin handshake check
   (the WebSocket CSRF control); cross-origin hosts must be listed explicitly in
   `pathland.allowed-origins` (comma-separated). The handshake `wid` is validated
   by server-core (`WindowIds`). SSR inherits SRI (`integrity="sha384-…"`) from
   `PathlandSession`. CSP/security headers and transport limits are documented in
   `docs/HARDENING.md` (Quarkus supplies secure defaults; Spring apps add them
   through Spring Security/server configuration).
 - **Hosted deployments work by default (issue #45 follow-up)**: a
   lowest-precedence `EnvironmentPostProcessor` contributes
   `server.forward-headers-strategy=framework`, so a TLS-terminating PaaS gets a
   correct WebSocket same-origin check and external SSR canonical URL with zero
   configuration. An explicit `server.forward-headers-strategy` in application
   config always wins (`ForwardedHeaderOverrideTest` pins this).
+- **Topic hub bean**: `PathlandAutoConfiguration` produces a `PathlandSignalHub`
+  bean (`host.signalHub()`: root mount, else the first mount) for external UI
+  updates. `TopicSubscriptionsTest` mounts a `/topics` app and proves a
+  background-thread publish reaches only the session subscribed for that subject.
 - **Java host / Kotlin views**: `KotlinViewMountTest` proves a Java-only
   `@SpringBootApplication` bean returning `PathlandApp` mounts a Kotlin-authored
   fixture view, renders it through SSR, and receives a live signal delta.
 
 - **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt.
 - **SEO document head (issue #45)**: the SSR controller derives the canonical
   URL from the request and passes host-default `PageMetadata` to the registry;
   `PathlandApp.pageMetadata(...)` may override it per route before the first
   paint. Canonical/OG/Twitter/JSON-LD are on by default and configurable via
   `pathland.seo.{enabled,site-name,image,og-type,twitter-card,twitter-site,structured-data}`.
 
 - **`PathlandAutoConfiguration`** (`@AutoConfiguration`, `@EnableWebSocket` since Spring
   Boot 3.5 no longer auto-enables it) + `META-INF/spring/…/AutoConfiguration.imports`:
   - default `StateStore` bean (`@ConditionalOnMissingBean` — Redis-or-in-memory),
   - `PathlandHost` bean (shut down with the context): every `MountedApp` bean plus the
     lone `PathlandApp` bean mounted at `/` (unless an explicit `MountedApp` claims the
     root). Without any app the host is empty and the starter is inert.
   - a `WebSocketConfigurer` registering **one handler per app** at its framework base
     (`/_pathland/ws` for the root, `/{mount}/_pathland/ws` otherwise). Each connection
     gets a fresh `uiId` (its UI model) + the client's `wid` (per-window state scope)
     from the WS `?wid=` query param (kept in `sessionStorage`, never in the page URL),
   - `PathlandIndexController` (SSR catch-all dispatching to the longest-mount app with
     the prefix stripped + a framework static controller serving the bundle + asset mount
     from `classpath:/static/_pathland/**` at both `/_pathland/**` and `/{app}/_pathland/**`;
     the more-specific mapping beats `/{*path}`, and the `!Upgrade` header excludes WS).
     When no static file matches, the controller serves renderer-owned assets from the
     shared Rust renderer: the content-hashed base stylesheet
     (`HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` at `baseCssName()`) as `text/css` with
     `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, and
     `/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg` glyphs (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` →
     `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an `immutable` cache header — no static CSS/icon
     files on any host, and a host can still override either with a file. SSR links
     the CSS via `PathlandSession` → `renderLinked`.
     The framework controller honors byte-range requests (`206 Partial Content` +
     `Content-Range`, `416` for unsatisfiable ranges, `Accept-Ranges` on the full
     response) — a `<video>` (a `MediaController`'s playback) seeking beyond its
     buffer issues a `Range`
     request, and answering it with a full `200` would make browsers restart the media
     at byte 0.
     SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS).
 - **SSR debug comments**: the host reads the `pathland.debug-html` property
   (`@Value("${pathland.debug-html:false}")`) and forwards it to each registry, enabling
   per-node HTML comments in SSR output when set.
 - **Per-window-id service worker (opt-in, issue #155)**: `pathland.service-worker`
   (default `false`) forwards to the host; the SSR emits `data-pathland-service-worker`
   and the controller serves `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` +
   `Cache-Control: no-cache` (a stable, uncached script the browser byte-compares).
 - **`SpringConnection`** — adapts `WebSocketSession` to `PathlandConnection`.
   `AutoCloseable`: a failed send surfaces as a close (the session's
   `closeConnection` closes the underlying session) so the DOM client reconnects +
   `META::RESYNC` instead of silently stalling on an open socket.
 - **Heartbeat** — the socket replies to a client `META::PING` with a `META::PONG`
   **at the transport layer** (through its `SpringConnection`, no actor/session
   dependency; spec/OPCODE.md §Transport heartbeat).
 - **Observability (issue #62)** — `spring-boot-starter-actuator` supplies the
   `MeterRegistry`; auto-config builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over it (decorated with
   `TracingTelemetry` when an `OpenTelemetry` bean is present — add
   `micrometer-tracing-bridge-otel` to opt in) and a `HealthIndicator` reporting the host
   UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/actuator/health`. The `pathland.*` meters are
   exposed at `/actuator/prometheus` (add `micrometer-registry-prometheus`).
 
 ## App DX
 
 ```java
 @SpringBootApplication
 public class MyApp {
     public static void main(String[] args) { SpringApplication.run(MyApp.class, args); }
     @Bean PathlandApp pathlandApp() { return () -> new MyHomeView(); }
     @Bean MountedApp support() { return MountedApp.of("/support", ...); } // optional 2nd app
 }
 ```
 
 ## Verified by
 
 `mvn test` — `PathlandAutoConfigurationTest` (`@SpringBootTest`): a `PathlandApp` bean
 mounts at `/` and SSR renders the root. `MultiSessionWebSocketTest`
 (`@SpringBootTest(RANDOM_PORT)`) opens **100 concurrent real WS sessions** against
 `/_pathland/ws` (via the shared `pathland-server-core` test-jar probe) and asserts each
 connects, re-syncs, gets transport-level PONGs, stays isolated, and is never closed by
 the peer. `PathlandObservabilityTest` (`@SpringBootTest` + `MockMvc`) asserts
 `/actuator/health` reports the `pathland` component UP and the auto-configured
 `PathlandTelemetry` is a `MicrometerTelemetry` registering `pathland.*` meters.
 `BaseCssHeadersTest` (`@SpringBootTest` + `MockMvc`) asserts the linked SSR
 `<link>`, the immutable `text/css` response at the global and mounted bases, and
 a 404 for an unknown hash.
 Manual: the `pathland-spring-boot-demo` renders `/`, `/kitchen`, `/settings`
 and the 404 fallback **and a second app at `/app2`**; a WebSocket handshake to
 `/_pathland/ws` and `/app2/_pathland/ws` returns 101.

@@ -0,0 +1,46 @@
+package dev.pathland.view.core.subscription
+
+import dev.pathland.view.core.signal.Signal
+
+/**
+ * The session-scoped surface available to views while they render: topic
+ * subscriptions and a way to schedule work on the session's actor.
+ *
+ * A live [SessionContext] is installed by the server runtime for the duration of
+ * every actor task (mount, dispatch, subscription drain, …), so [Topic] reads can
+ * resolve without any explicit plumbing. Outside a session (an emitter-only unit
+ * test, for example) [current] is `null`.
+ */
+interface SessionContext {
+
+    /** Subscribe to [topic] for [subject], seeded with [initial]. Idempotent per `(topic, subject)`. */
+    fun <T, S> subscribe(topic: Topic<T, S>, subject: S, initial: T): Signal<T>
+
+    /** Drop the session's subscription for `(topic, subject)`. */
+    fun <T, S> unsubscribe(topic: Topic<T, S>, subject: S)
+
+    /** Run [task] on this session's actor (never on the caller's thread). */
+    fun submit(task: Runnable)
+
+    companion object {
+        private val CURRENT = ThreadLocal<SessionContext?>()
+
+        /** The session context of the current actor task, or `null`. */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun current(): SessionContext? = CURRENT.get()
+
+        /** Install [context] for the current thread; returns the previous one. */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun push(context: SessionContext): SessionContext? {
+            val previous = CURRENT.get()
+            CURRENT.set(context)
+            return previous
+        }
+
+        /** Restore the context returned by [push]. */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun restore(previous: SessionContext?) {
+            if (previous == null) CURRENT.remove() else CURRENT.set(previous)
+        }
+    }
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,31 @@
+package dev.pathland.view.core.subscription
+
+/**
+ * A strongly typed, always-scoped subscription key.
+ *
+ * [T] is the published payload type and [S] is the subject (the thing the
+ * subscription is about — a customer id, order id, tenant, conversation, …).
+ * Both are checked at compile time by [subscribe] and
+ * `PathlandSignalHub.publish`.
+ *
+ * Identity is by [name] (not by instance), so a topic declared once and shared
+ * across modules — or across a process boundary — resolves to the same
+ * subscription stream. Two topics with the same name must therefore carry the
+ * same payload and subject types; declare each topic once in a shared constant
+ * object.
+ */
+class Topic<T, S>(@JvmField val name: String) {
+
+    override fun equals(other: Any?): Boolean =
+        this === other || (other is Topic<*, *> && other.name == name)
+
+    override fun hashCode(): Int = name.hashCode()
+
+    override fun toString(): String = "Topic($name)"
+
+    companion object {
+        /** A topic named [name] with payload type [T] and subject type [S]. */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun <T, S> of(name: String): Topic<T, S> = Topic(name)
+    }
+}
